correctness.rationale: The real Hermitian trace-norm unit ball reduces the norm to pure inputs, and local-unitary covariance makes every qubit–qudit pure input Schmidt-equivalent to a one-parameter state. The exact output spectrum is a Hermitian two-by-two block with eigenvalues \(\frac14\pm\frac12\sqrt{1-bu^2}\), two nonpositive diagonal entries with total absolute mass \(\frac12\), and \(n-2\) pairs of eigenvalues \(\pm u/(2n)\). The resulting trace norm is \(\frac12+cu+\max\{\frac12,\sqrt{1-bu^2}\}\). Its square-root branch is strictly concave with a unique admissible optimum at \(c/\sqrt{b(b+c^2)}\), and this beats the linear branch for every \(c=(n-2)/n\in[0,1)\) by \(\frac34-c+\frac{c^4}{4b}\ge\frac{(1-c)^2(c^2+2c+3)}4>0\). Trace duality yields the spectral norm, and a product-state tensor calculation plus convexity gives the sharp separable bound. The standalone checker independently replayed 958 finite numerical assertions; they are supplementary to the analytic proof for all integers in the domain.

value.rationale: The real-Hermitian tensor correlation projection is a natural second-order Banach-space operator and entanglement observable. The theorem is the exact endpoint norm for every qubit–qudit dimension, identifies unique optimal Schmidt coefficients and establishes a strict separable-versus-entangled trace norm gap, yielding a sharp sufficient entanglement witness. The first-order marginal projection has different optimizer geometry; hence the new all-n phenomenon is motivated and not merely a local substitution. No claim of a universal entanglement detector or general higher-local-dimension extension is made.
